findings.title: Completion logs no longer record unsampled trace IDs
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware used to attach traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false), which includes unsampled spans. That field was removed and the line now only calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info. Infra FromContext only adds traceID for sampled spans (TraceIDFromContext with requireSampled=true). Plugin Request Completed logs for unsampled requests therefore lose traceID, so those requests can no longer be correlated from the egress log.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext drops the fake and the context
findings.body: FromContext ignores both the receiver and the context and returns NewTestLogger(). LoggerMiddleware now logs via logger.FromContext(ctx).Info, so any test that injects *TestLogger will record nothing on the instance under assertion: Calls, Message, and Ctx stay on a discarded logger. Contextual attributes also cannot be observed. The fake must return itself (or a child that shares the same Logs) and retain the context key/values.

findings.title: No test that contextual fields still reach the completion log
findings.body: pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, and dsUID were removed from LoggerMiddleware's explicit log params and now depend on ContextualLoggerMiddleware calling log.WithContextualAttributes before LoggerMiddleware's FromContext. Nothing in this PR tests that middleware, a nil-safe request, or that Plugin Request Completed still contains those fields when the two middlewares are stacked as in CreateMiddlewares. A reversed wrap order or a FromContext that does not merge contextual attributes would silently drop datasource and plugin identity from egress logs.
